clue.text: Some Tesco-read bands to decipher?

indicators.note: deciphering means sorting jumbled characters into sense, so the selected letters are rearranged
only some of the letters of the phrase Tesco-read bands are kept, the stretch from its middle, the rest dropped

explanation.surface: A shopper wonders whether the striped labels a supermarket scanner reads are a code waiting to be cracked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' keeps COREADB from the middle of 'Tesco-read bands' (dropping TES and ANDS), and 'to decipher' rearranges those letters. The whole clue also describes the answer, so it is an &lit.
explanation.definitionFit: The striped labels that checkout scanners read are exactly what a shop's tills decode to identify each product.

clue.text: Attributed to political extremists always, lesser action

parts.note: a work by someone is attributed to them

indicators.note: extremists here are the extreme letters of political, its first and last

parts.note: ay, a variant of aye, means always or ever

explanation.surface: Something credited to radicals forever is a minor bit of action.
explanation.definitionFit: Secondary stage business going on beside the main action in a play is minor activity.

clue.text: Tool putting inscription on tombstone, a motto

parts.note: RIP, rest in peace, is carved on gravestones
a saw is an old saying or motto

explanation.surface: An implement for carving an epitaph and a motto onto a gravestone.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a coarse hand-saw used for cutting wood along the grain, a carpenter's implement.

clue.text: At dinner time, food is thus submitted for consideration

definitions.text: At dinner time, food is thus
definitions.meaning: at mealtime the food sits on the dining surface
a proposal laid open for discussion

explanation.surface: At mealtime the food is presented, as a proposal might be.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a plan put forward for discussion, and literally food placed for eating.

clue.text: Entering vortex, travelling further

indicators.note: the answer is entering, placed within, the words vortex travelling

explanation.surface: Going into a whirlpool means travelling further on.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean additional or more, as in more time or added time.

clue.text: Married, husband proved irritating

parts.note: something that itched was irritating, as an itchy rash proves

explanation.surface: A wife complains that her new spouse turned out to be an annoyance.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting hitched is an informal idiom for getting married, so hitched means wed.

clue.text: In time, Ireland abandoned uncompromising leader

indicators.note: in puts the jumbled letters inside the abbreviation for time

parts.note: HR is short for hour, a unit of time

indicators.note: abandoned suggests wild, unrestrained, so the letters run riot

explanation.surface: A tough politician eventually left the Irish republic behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who rigidly sticks to a strict policy, such as an unbending party chief, is this.

clue.text: Food and drink, lake, for duck

parts.note: tea is both a drink and a light afternoon meal
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Bread, water and a pond provided for a waterbird.
explanation.definitionFit: A small freshwater dabbling waterfowl with a green wing patch is one species.

clue.text: President from nation needing leadership in Europe

parts.note: Holland is a common name for the Netherlands

indicators.note: leadership in Europe is its leading letter

explanation.surface: A head of state from a country needing to lead within the EU.
explanation.walkthrough: François Hollande was President of France at the time of this puzzle (2016).
explanation.definitionFit: He was French head of state from 2012 to 2017.

clue.text: Change character, seeing awful starter filling plate

indicators.note: filling puts a letter into the middle of the word, like a filling in a tooth

parts.note: a dental plate holds false teeth, a denture

indicators.note: starter is the first letter of awful

explanation.surface: A dentist sees a dreadful first course stuck in some false teeth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plate' is a dental plate, not dinnerware.
explanation.definitionFit: To alter the nature of something, as a protein is altered by heat, is to change its character.

clue.text: Bird of about 6.28 feet, no charge

parts.note: pi is about 3.14, so two of it make roughly 6.28

indicators.note: no tells us that the word for a charge is to be removed from the word feet

parts.note: a fee is a charge for a service

explanation.surface: A puzzling description of a bird roughly two metres long that costs nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking FEE from FEET leaves just T.
explanation.definitionFit: The pipit is a small brown songbird related to wagtails and resembling a lark.

clue.text: Setter at sea, perhaps, wearing something waterproof

parts.note: a tar is a sailor, someone typically found at sea
Paul is the pseudonym of this puzzle's setter
if you are in a coat you are wearing it

explanation.surface: The puzzle's compiler, out on the ocean, has put on oilskins.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul is the setter's Guardian pseudonym, which is why 'Setter' gives PAUL here.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarpaulin is a heavy waterproof sheet of canvas used to cover things from the rain.

clue.text: A puzzle with cojones, brilliant!

parts.note: a maze is a puzzle of winding paths
cojones is Spanish slang for testicles, in English balls

explanation.surface: Praise for a bold, gutsy crossword: what a great puzzle!
explanation.definitionFit: A slangy exclamation of delight, meaning fantastic or wonderful, much like awesome.

clue.text: A pink organ moving towards the rear

parts.note: the Financial Times, printed on pink paper, is a newspaper or organ, abbreviated FT

explanation.surface: Something flesh-coloured inside the body shifts backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' here is a newspaper: the Financial Times is famously printed on salmon-pink paper.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship the word means at or toward the stern, the back end of the vessel.

clue.text: Evidence of excitement, as energy feels so incredibly hot

parts.note: go means energy or vigour

indicators.note: incredibly suggests the letters of feels so are rearranged beyond belief

parts.note: H is the tap abbreviation for hot

explanation.surface: A lively person feels unbelievably warm.
explanation.definitionFit: Bumpy skin raised from thrill or fear, also called goosebumps, shows excitement.

clue.text: Legal directive good, ruling ultimately welcomed by brotherhood of elders?

indicators.note: being welcomed by something puts you within it, so a letter goes inside

parts.note: a whimsical order or fraternity of ageing people, an ageing order

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word ruling

explanation.surface: A council of senior figures approves a good court ruling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brotherhood of elders?' is a playful invention, an order of people who are ageing, spelt AGING ORDER.
explanation.definitionFit: A court injunction forbidding public discussion or reporting of a matter is a legal directive.

clue.text: Wall ornament aligned or skew-whiff

indicators.note: skew-whiff means askew or crooked, so the letters are knocked out of line

explanation.surface: A decorative wall fixture that is straight or crooked.
explanation.walkthrough: Skew-whiff is British slang for crooked.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a branched candlestick bracket mounted on a wall, a decorative fixture.

clue.text: Letter from Dalmatian port's read out — one's in the soup

parts.note: Split is a port on Croatia's Dalmatian coast

indicators.note: read out says the letter is pronounced, giving its name

parts.note: P is a letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A letter posted from a Croatian harbour town is read aloud by someone in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the soup' looks like the idiom for in trouble; it is meant literally, an ingredient of soup.
explanation.definitionFit: Dried halved peas are a classic ingredient of thick soups such as pea and ham.

clue.text: Lighter grip, one's loose

indicators.note: loose means not fixed, so the letters are freed to move

explanation.surface: A slacker hold means a person's grip has come loose.
explanation.definitionFit: More porous and light, like a sponge cake that is airier than another.

clue.text: Sun etc in before this, brightness ends

parts.note: something in is fashionable, or popular
pre is a prefix meaning before

indicators.note: ends picks out the final letters of the words this and brightness

explanation.surface: The sun's glow fades just before this moment, a bit of weather talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sun' is the British tabloid newspaper, not the star. 'ends' takes the last letters of 'this' and 'brightness'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sun is one of Britain's mass-market tabloid newspapers, an example of the tabloids collectively.

clue.text: Bird in brief dive, gull

indicators.note: brief means cut short, so the final letter is lost

parts.note: a fall is a dive or plunge
to gull is to dupe or con

explanation.surface: A bird in a short swoop, like a seagull.
explanation.definitionFit: A swift diurnal bird of prey, such as the peregrine, is this kind of raptor.

clue.text: Fruit, simian ecstasy

parts.note: an orang, short for orang-utan, is an ape
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A fruit that sends an ape into raptures.
explanation.definitionFit: A round citrus fruit, sweet and juicy, is one example.

clue.text: Charged particle nothing to write home about

indicators.note: the word for home goes about, around, the letter for nothing

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A tiny charged speck is dismissed as unremarkable.
explanation.definitionFit: An atom or molecule that has gained or lost electrons carries a net electric charge.

clue.text: Snigger repeatedly if, on man, a bra regularly seen

indicators.note: repeatedly says the snigger is given twice over
regularly picks every other letter of the words if on man a bra

explanation.surface: Someone giggles over and over on seeing a man in a bra.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the leering laugh of the 1980s British comic strip Finbarr Saunders in Viz.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the smutty schoolboy chuckle at innuendo, a written-out snigger.

clue.text: Ship left Spain for famous Irish bay

parts.note: Noah's ark is a ship
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A vessel sailed from Spain toward a celebrated Irish inlet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bay' looks like a coastal inlet but means a bay horse: Arkle was a great Irish steeplechaser of the 1960s.
explanation.definitionFit: Arkle, a bay-coloured racehorse, won three Cheltenham Gold Cups and is Ireland's most celebrated chaser.

clue.text: Boss in brief survey

indicators.note: brief means shortened, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a study is a survey or examination

explanation.surface: A manager appears in a short report.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss can be a raised knob or ornamental stud, as on a shield.

clue.text: Discomfort with provocative dance reported as an act of touching up?

indicators.note: reported means the words are as heard when spoken

parts.note: discomfort is pain, and twerking is a provocative bottom-shaking dance, so pain plus twerk

explanation.surface: A painful, suggestive dance is described as groping someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touching up' looks like sexual groping, but here it means retouching paint.
explanation.definitionFit: Retouched surfaces of a car or house are its painted finish, so touching up is a pun on fresh coats.

clue.text: About ninety, one exercising, one having done a stretch?

indicators.note: about means around, so the shuffled letters surround the numeral
exercising works the letters of one about, rearranging them

parts.note: XC is ninety in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A nonagenarian at the gym, doing stretches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stretch' suggests exercise, but here it is a term in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretch is slang for a jail sentence, so a former prisoner has done one.

clue.text: A game of tricks cut short

parts.note: bridge is a card game played by taking tricks

explanation.surface: A conjuring routine, or a card game, is ended early.
explanation.definitionFit: To condense a book or text is to shorten it, keeping the essentials.

clue.text: Better to spray henna on coarse skin

indicators.note: to spray is to scatter, so the letters of henna are scattered about
skin is the outside, the first and last letters of coarse

explanation.surface: Advice that misting henna onto rough skin will improve it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to improve something, making it of higher quality.
